issues.legal_issue: Manufacture of a commercially distinct product from a mined mineral is not processing of the mineral within the extended definition of a mine for electricity-duty classification.
material_facts: Electricity was used at facilities that processed mined ore and at facilities that used the ore as an input, together with other materials, to manufacture a different commercial product.
The ore-processing facilities removed impurities or enriched the mineral while preserving its identity as a mineral.
The manufacturing processes, including smelting, transformed the mined material into products with a distinct commercial identity and different physical or chemical characteristics.
The dispute concerned whether electricity used in those manufacturing processes attracted the duty rate applicable to mines or the rate applicable to manufacturing units.
issues.conclusion: The manufacturing facilities producing a new and distinct commercial product from mined minerals do not fall within the extended definition of a mine; electricity used there is subject to the rate applicable to manufacturing units.
issues.legal_principle: Under Explanation (b) to Part B of the table in Section 3(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Electricity Duty Act, 1949, the words “crushing, processing, treating or transporting the mineral” refer to activities connected with the mined mineral that do not substantially change its identity. Applying noscitur a sociis, as discussed in Rohit Pulp and Paper Mills Ltd. v. Collector of Central Excise and Ahmedabad Pvt. Primary Teachers’ Association v. Administrative Officer, “processing” takes its meaning from the associated words and does not extend to manufacture of a different product. The distinction between processing and manufacture is supported by CIT v. Tara Agency, Orient Paper and Industries v. State of M.P., Aspinwall & Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income Tax, and Servo-Med Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Central Excise: manufacture occurs when processing transforms material into a commercially distinct article.

rule.if: electricity_duty_classification_dispute and mined_mineral_used_as_raw_material and manufacturing_transforms_mineral and distinct_commercial_product_created

predicates.electricity_duty_classification_dispute: The case concerns how electricity use at facilities connected with mining is classified for electricity-duty purposes.
predicates.mined_mineral_used_as_raw_material: The facility uses a mineral obtained by mining as an input to its operations.
predicates.manufacturing_transforms_mineral: The facility carries out a manufacturing process that substantially changes the mined mineral rather than merely preparing it for sale or transport.
predicates.distinct_commercial_product_created: The process produces an article recognized commercially as different from the mined mineral.

issues.definition: When an electricity-duty classification dispute concerns a facility that uses a mined mineral as raw material and manufactures a commercially distinct product by substantially transforming it, the facility is treated as a manufacturing unit rather than as an extended mine.
